# Per-worker tokens

<!-- Generated by `go run docs/roadmap/gen.go docs` from tickets.json. Do not edit by hand. -->

**Phase:** [P1 · Who did it](../README.md#phase-1--who-did-it) · **Lane:** Control plane · **Label:** `feature:worker-credentials` · **Epic:** [#50](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/50) · **Tickets:** 6 (3S 3M)

The control plane issues a separate token for each worker. The token is shown once, stored only as a hash, bound to a proxy id (or a proxy id prefix for replica pools), revocable and tracked by last use. Workers use it for /policy, /control/heartbeat and /central/ingest, and the token's bound proxy id becomes the identity the CP trusts instead of the self-reported header. The shared WARDEN_CP_TOKEN is retired through an explicit auth mode and a documented migration. Workers need no code change: both `controlPlane.tokenEnv` and `central.tokenEnv` carry the worker's own token.

## How we build it

- Token format: `wwt_` + lowercase unpadded RFC 4648 base32 of 32 crypto/rand bytes (52 characters after the prefix). Token id: `wt_` + 16 hex characters. The CP stores only sha256(token), which is enough for 256-bit random secrets. New cpstate migration `worker_tokens(id, name UNIQUE, proxy_id, proxy_id_prefix, token_hash UNIQUE, created_by, created_at, expires_at NULL, last_used_at NULL, revoked_at NULL, revoked_by NULL)`. Exactly one of proxy_id and proxy_id_prefix is set, chosen at create time. At most 2 active tokens per binding, so rotation can overlap. Plaintext is returned only by Create and never logged, audited, stored or returned by any GET.
- Requires cpstate, which exists only with --state-dir (W-P1-SSO-01). One resolver picks the worker auth mode at startup and logs it once: `open` (no legacy token, not strict: today's behaviour, anonymous callers accepted as kind=none, warning logged), `mixed` (legacy token configured: worker tokens or the legacy token, anonymous rejected), `strict` (`--require-worker-tokens`: worker tokens only). Strict without --state-dir, or strict together with a legacy token, fails startup. Strict without TLS fails startup unless `--allow-insecure-worker-auth` is set; any token mode without TLS logs a warning.
- Seam: `WorkerAuthenticator.Authenticate(r) (WorkerPrincipal{TokenID, TokenName, ProxyID, Kind token|legacy|none}, error)`, applied only to /policy, /control/heartbeat and /central/ingest. It replaces `policyServer.token`, the bearerOK call in `handleHeartbeat`, and the string token in `analytics.NewIngestHandler` (which takes an authorizer func; `analytics.StaticTokenAuthorizer` keeps the old behaviour for the worker's own aggregator at internal/worker/worker.go:450). `bearerOK` stays on /central/secrets under W-P1-SSO-06 rules. A `wwt_` bearer is never accepted on /central/secrets, /dashboard/* or /auth/*. A `wwt_` bearer goes only through the token path and never falls back to the legacy compare.
- Identity: for kind=token the principal's ProxyID is authoritative. Missing X-Warden-Proxy-ID resolves to the bound proxy_id (a prefix-bound token requires the header). A header equal to the bound id, or matching the bound prefix, is accepted; any other value gets 403. The registry (SeenPolicyPull, SeenHeartbeat, SeenIngest), the stored AggregatedEvent.ProxyID and the ingest/events/MCP/secrets callbacks use the principal's id, never the raw header. Legacy and none principals keep using the header and are shown as unverified.
- Hot path: an in-memory index from hash to token is the only per-request lookup (one sha256 and one map read, no DB I/O). It is rebuilt after in-process Create/Revoke and reloaded when a 2s poll of SQLite `PRAGMA data_version` changes, which picks up writes from the bootstrap CLI process. A reload error keeps the last good index and never fails open. expires_at is checked against the CP clock only. `last_used_at` is updated in memory and flushed in one transaction every 60s and on shutdown.
- Revocation is a soft delete (revoked_at set, row kept). Every /policy response (200 or 304) is re-authenticated before it is written, and an in-process revoke cancels that token's held long-polls through a per-token cancel registry so they return 401 at once. Bounds: API revoke takes effect on the next request; CLI revoke within 2s. Missing, malformed, unknown, expired and revoked tokens all get the same 401 body `unauthorized` with `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer`; a binding failure gets 403 `proxy id mismatch`. The reason goes only to a rate-limited `worker auth rejected` log line, never the token or its hash.
- Admin surfaces: `GET/POST /dashboard/api/worker-tokens` and `DELETE /dashboard/api/worker-tokens/{id}`, admin role through the W-P1-SSO-05 authz table. With console.auth=none, POST and DELETE return 403 pointing to the CLI. The offline CLI `warden control-plane token create|list|revoke --state-dir` works with or without a running CP. `create --from-env VAR|--from-file F` registers an operator-generated `wwt_` value (format checked, only the hash stored), so compose and Kubernetes Secrets can supply the value; re-running it with the same name and value is a no-op.
- Audit: only token create and revoke are admin-audit events (target `worker_tokens`, auth_method oidc|breakglass|cli). Worker-plane routes (/policy, /control/heartbeat, /central/ingest) are excluded from the W-P1-AAUD-02 middleware. CLI appends must keep the chain linear across processes (append inside a SQLite `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` transaction that reads prev_hash inside it).
- Observability: dashboard.WorkerView gains `tokenName`, `tokenLastUsed`, `authKind` (token|legacy|none) and `legacyRequests`; the fleet view shows a legacy/unverified badge. The CP has no /metrics endpoint in P1, so an in-memory counter `warden_cp_worker_auth_total{kind,outcome}` (bounded labels, no proxy_id) is kept and exported when the CP metrics endpoint lands (W-P5-RETN-06). Legacy request tracking per proxy id is capped at 10,000 ids.
- Migration: `--legacy-token-env` (with `--token-env` kept as a deprecated alias) keeps the shared token working, so an upgraded CP behaves as before until tokens are issued. In strict mode with console.auth=none, /central/secrets is not mounted, because its only gate would otherwise be an empty shared token. A revoked worker keeps enforcing its last-known-good, default-deny policy, gets no updates and cannot heartbeat or ingest; stopping its traffic means stopping the worker. Hand-off to P2: W-P2-WCA-04 extends WorkerAuthenticator with mTLS principals, and /central/secrets stays a human route in both phases.

## Done when

On a CP running with --state-dir and TLS, two workers use distinct per-worker tokens, one created in the console and one with the bootstrap CLI against the running CP. Each worker's /policy, heartbeat and ingest succeed with no worker code change, and events and fleet rows are attributed to each token's bound proxy id; a request with a spoofed X-Warden-Proxy-ID gets 403. A worker token is rejected on /central/secrets. Revoking one token in the console makes its next request on all three endpoints return 401 and a held long-poll return 401 at once; a CLI revoke takes effect within 2s. The other worker keeps working, and the revoked worker keeps its last-known-good default-deny policy. Tokens and revocations survive a CP restart. Create and revoke appear in the admin audit log with the correct actor, and worker-plane traffic does not. The plaintext appears only in the create response or CLI output. A CP started with --require-worker-tokens logs auth_mode=strict, rejects WARDEN_CP_TOKEN with 401 and refuses to start without --state-dir. The control-plane compose recipe comes up with per-worker tokens and no WARDEN_CP_TOKEN.

### 1/6 · W-P1-WTOK-01

**Add worker token store with hashed storage, revocation and in-memory index**

Type **feature** · Size **M** · Issue [#51](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/51)

Add the `worker_tokens` cpstate migration and a `WorkerTokenStore` in internal/controlplane that creates, authenticates, revokes and lists per-worker tokens. Only sha256 of the token is stored, and the plaintext is returned once by Create. Authentication reads an in-memory index so the request path does no DB I/O, and the index reloads when another process (the bootstrap CLI) writes the same SQLite file. Nothing calls the store yet, so this merges with no behaviour change.

**Requirements**

- Migration `worker_tokens(id TEXT PK, name TEXT UNIQUE NOT NULL, proxy_id TEXT NULL, proxy_id_prefix TEXT NULL, token_hash BLOB UNIQUE NOT NULL, created_by TEXT NOT NULL, created_at, expires_at NULL, last_used_at NULL, revoked_at NULL, revoked_by NULL)` with a CHECK that exactly one of proxy_id and proxy_id_prefix is set, registered through the internal/cpstate migration runner (W-P1-SSO-01). Without --state-dir no store exists.
- Token = `wwt_` + lowercase unpadded base32 of 32 crypto/rand bytes; id = `wt_` + 16 hex; name 1-64 characters; proxy_id and prefix match `^[A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,128}$`. Malformed input is rejected before hashing or any lookup.
- API: `Create(ctx, CreateOpts{Name, ProxyID, ProxyIDPrefix, ExpiresAt, Actor, Plaintext})` returns (plaintext, Token, error); an empty Plaintext generates one, a supplied one is format-checked and registered (import). `Authenticate(plaintext)` returns Token or ErrMalformed/ErrUnknown/ErrRevoked/ErrExpired. `Revoke(ctx, id, actor)` is idempotent and returns ErrNotFound for an unknown id. `List(ctx)` returns metadata only. `MarkUsed(id, t)`.
- At most 2 active (not revoked, not expired) tokens per binding; a third Create returns ErrTooManyActive. Create with an existing name returns ErrNameTaken, unless it is an import whose name and hash match an active row, which is a no-op.
- Authenticate reads only an in-memory hash-to-token index. The index is rebuilt after in-process Create/Revoke and reloaded when `PRAGMA data_version` changes (polled every 2s by `Run(ctx)`); a reload error keeps the last good index and logs a warning. Expiry uses the CP clock.
- MarkUsed updates memory only; dirty last_used_at values are flushed in one transaction every 60s (interval injectable for tests) and by `Flush(ctx)` on shutdown.
- Token.String() and slog LogValue print only id, name and binding. No log, error message or test output contains the plaintext or the hash.

**Implementation plan**

1. internal/cpstate (from W-P1-SSO-01): register a new `worker_tokens` migration with indexes on proxy_id and proxy_id_prefix.
2. New file internal/controlplane/workertokens.go: types Token, CreateOpts, the error values, and `NewWorkerTokenStore(db *cpstate.DB, opts StoreOptions) (*WorkerTokenStore, error)` that loads the index.
3. Implement Create (generate or import, validate, enforce the active-per-binding limit, insert, update index), Revoke (soft delete, update index), List and Authenticate (prefix and length check, sha256, map read, revoked/expired checks).
4. Implement `Run(ctx)`: a ticker that reads `PRAGMA data_version` every 2s and reloads the index on change, and flushes MarkUsed state every 60s; implement `Flush(ctx)`.
5. Add a `Changes()`-style internal hook (unexported for now) so a later Postgres backend can replace data_version polling without changing callers.
6. New file internal/controlplane/workertokens_test.go and a benchmark BenchmarkWorkerTokenAuthenticate.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] Given a created token, the DB file does not contain the plaintext (bytes.Contains on the file) and token_hash equals sha256(plaintext).
- [ ] Authenticate returns ErrRevoked for a revoked token, ErrExpired after expires_at (fake clock), ErrUnknown for a well-formed unknown token, and ErrMalformed for a value without the `wwt_` prefix or with the wrong length.
- [ ] A token created and then revoked through a second WorkerTokenStore on the same DB file (the CLI case) authenticates and then fails with ErrRevoked in the first store within one 2s poll interval.
- [ ] 10,000 MarkUsed calls for 3 tokens in one interval produce exactly one write transaction, and Flush writes pending values.
- [ ] A third active token for the same proxy_id returns ErrTooManyActive; re-importing the same name and value is a no-op.
- [ ] `go test -race ./internal/controlplane -run TestWorkerTokenStore` passes and `go test ./internal/controlplane -run '^$' -bench BenchmarkWorkerTokenAuthenticate` reports a cache-hit lookup under 50µs/op.

**Depends on:** [`W-P1-SSO-01`](console-sso-rbac.md#18--w-p1-sso-01) Add internal/cpstate SQLite state store with migrations

**Unblocks:** [`W-P1-WTOK-02`](worker-credentials.md#26--w-p1-wtok-02) Authenticate /policy, heartbeat and ingest with per-worker tokens; [`W-P1-WTOK-05`](worker-credentials.md#56--w-p1-wtok-05) Add offline worker token bootstrap CLI; [`W-P1-OPS1-04`](ops-hardening.md#44--w-p1-ops1-04) Add CP state-dir lock and verified restore command

### 2/6 · W-P1-WTOK-02

**Authenticate /policy, heartbeat and ingest with per-worker tokens**

Type **feature** · Size **M** · Issue [#52](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/52)

Add `WorkerAuthenticator` in internal/controlplane and apply it once to /policy, /control/heartbeat and /central/ingest, replacing the three separate shared-token checks. The token's bound proxy id becomes the identity the registry and ingest store record. The default mode stays as today: with no worker tokens issued, a CP with --token-env behaves exactly as before, and a CP with no token and no state stays open with a warning. /central/secrets keeps its own gate and never accepts a worker token.

**Requirements**

- `WorkerAuthenticator.Authenticate(r *http.Request) (WorkerPrincipal, error)` with `WorkerPrincipal{TokenID, TokenName, ProxyID, Kind}` (Kind token|legacy|none). A `wwt_` bearer goes only to WorkerTokenStore; any other bearer is compared in constant time with the legacy token; mode is resolved once at startup (open, mixed, strict) and logged as `auth_mode=...`.
- Applied only to /policy, /control/heartbeat and /central/ingest. bearerOK remains only on /central/secrets, and a `wwt_` bearer there gets 401 for every method.
- Binding: for kind=token a missing X-Warden-Proxy-ID resolves to the bound proxy_id; a matching header (or prefix match) is accepted; anything else gets 403 `proxy id mismatch`. The registry and the ingest store always receive principal.ProxyID.
- `analytics.NewIngestHandler(store, auth func(*http.Request) (proxyID string, status int))`; the returned proxyID is used for AggregatedEvent.ProxyID and every ingest callback. `analytics.StaticTokenAuthorizer(token)` keeps the old behaviour for internal/worker/worker.go:450 and existing tests.
- ServePolicy re-authenticates before writing any response (200 and 304) after a wait; an in-process revoke cancels that token's held long-polls through a per-token cancel registry so they return 401 within 1s. Waking N waiters does no DB I/O.
- Missing, malformed, unknown, expired and revoked tokens get the same 401 body `unauthorized` and `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer`. Rejections log `worker auth rejected` with reason, token_id when known and remote_addr, at most once per reason and remote_addr per minute; the Authorization header, plaintext and hash are never logged.
- Successful requests call MarkUsed and record Kind and TokenID on the registry entry; in-memory counters `warden_cp_worker_auth_total{kind,outcome}` are kept for later export.

**Implementation plan**

1. New file internal/controlplane/workerauth.go: WorkerPrincipal, WorkerAuthenticator, the mode resolver, the binding check, the rate-limited rejection logger and the per-token cancel registry.
2. internal/analytics/central_http.go: change NewIngestHandler to take the authorizer func and use its proxyID instead of `r.Header.Get(ProxyIDHeader)`; add StaticTokenAuthorizer; update internal/worker/worker.go:450 and the analytics tests to use it.
3. internal/controlplane/policyserver.go: replace the `token` field and the inline compare in ServePolicy with the authenticator; re-authenticate before both StatusNotModified writes and the 200 write; select on the token's cancel channel; call registry.SeenPolicyPull(principal.ProxyID).
4. internal/controlplane/controlplane.go: add `Config.WorkerTokens *WorkerTokenStore` (nil without state); build the authenticator in New(); use it in handleHeartbeat instead of bearerOK; wire ingest with an adapter; leave bearerOK on handleSecrets/handleSecretByKey and reject `wwt_` bearers there.
5. internal/controlplane/registry.go: record Kind, TokenID and a legacy request count on SeenPolicyPull, SeenHeartbeat and SeenIngest.
6. cmd/proxy/controlplane.go: when cpstate is open, construct the store, start Run(ctx), Flush on shutdown, and log the resolved mode.
7. Tests in internal/controlplane/workerauth_test.go: a table over the three routes for valid, mismatched, missing-header, revoked and legacy cases, a long-poll revoke test, and a /central/secrets rejection test.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] Token A bound to `worker-1` with header `worker-2` gets 403 on all three endpoints; without the header all three succeed and the registry lists `worker-1`.
- [ ] After A is revoked, its next request on each endpoint returns 401 with body `unauthorized`, while token B for `worker-2` keeps getting 200/204.
- [ ] A held `GET /policy?wait=30s` for token A returns 401 within 1s of revoking A, and a revoked token whose wait times out gets 401, not 304.
- [ ] A valid `wwt_` token gets 401 on POST, GET and DELETE /central/secrets.
- [ ] An ingest batch sent with token A and no header is stored with AggregatedEvent.ProxyID `worker-1`.
- [ ] Existing shared-token tests pass unchanged: `go test -race ./internal/controlplane -run 'TestWorkerAuth|TestPolicyTokenAuth|TestHeartbeatEndpoint|TestLongPollETag'` and `go test ./internal/analytics -run 'TestCentralIngest|TestIngest'`.

**Depends on:** [`W-P1-WTOK-01`](worker-credentials.md#16--w-p1-wtok-01) Add worker token store with hashed storage, revocation and in-memory index

**Unblocks:** [`W-P1-WTOK-03`](worker-credentials.md#36--w-p1-wtok-03) Add worker token admin API, dashboard panel and fleet auth fields; [`W-P2-APIK-02`](api-keys.md#27--w-p2-apik-02) Authenticate API keys and enforce per-route scopes in the authz table

### 3/6 · W-P1-WTOK-03

**Add worker token admin API, dashboard panel and fleet auth fields**

Type **feature** · Size **M** · Issue [#53](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/53)

Add the admin API and a console panel to create, list and revoke worker tokens, and show each worker's auth kind in the fleet view. The plaintext is returned once, with `Cache-Control: no-store`, and never again. Mutations need the admin role and are recorded by the admin audit middleware, which must not record worker-plane traffic. The offline bootstrap CLI is W-P1-WTOK-05.

**Requirements**

- `GET /dashboard/api/worker-tokens` returns 200 `[{id,name,proxyID,proxyIDPrefix,createdBy,createdAt,expiresAt,lastUsedAt,revokedAt}]`, including revoked tokens, never the hash or plaintext.
- `POST /dashboard/api/worker-tokens` with `{name, proxyID|proxyIDPrefix, expiresIn?}` returns 201 `{id,name,...,token}` with `Cache-Control: no-store`; 400 for invalid input, 409 for a taken name or too many active tokens. `DELETE /dashboard/api/worker-tokens/{id}` soft-revokes and returns 204, or 404 for an unknown id.
- Routes are wired through a new `dashboard.Server.SetWorkerTokens(...)` setter (not mounted on workers) and have admin entries in the W-P1-SSO-05 authz table. With console.auth=none, POST and DELETE return 403 with a message pointing to the CLI; GET is allowed.
- dashboard.WorkerView gains `tokenName`, `tokenLastUsed`, `authKind` (token|legacy|none) and `legacyRequests`, filled from the registry; the fleet panel shows a legacy or unverified badge.
- Create and revoke are audited by the W-P1-AAUD-02 middleware with target `worker_tokens`; the registered StateHasher hashes metadata only. /policy, /control/heartbeat and /central/ingest are excluded from that middleware.
- The index.html panel shows the token once with a copy button and hides write controls for non-admins based on /auth/me.

**Implementation plan**

1. New file internal/dashboard/dashboard_workertokens.go: a WorkerTokenAdmin interface, Server.SetWorkerTokens, handleWorkerTokens (GET/POST) and handleWorkerTokenByID (DELETE); register in dashboard.go Handler() next to /dashboard/api/workers.
2. internal/dashboard/dashboard.go: extend WorkerView with the new fields.
3. internal/controlplane/controlplane.go: pass the WorkerTokenStore adapter to SetWorkerTokens and fill the new WorkerView fields in the SetWorkers closure.
4. Add the three routes to the W-P1-SSO-05 authz table; register the worker_tokens StateHasher; confirm with a test that the W-P1-AAUD-02 middleware never wraps /policy, /control/heartbeat or /central/ingest.
5. internal/dashboard/index.html: add the Worker tokens panel and the fleet badge.
6. Tests in internal/dashboard/dashboard_workertokens_test.go and internal/controlplane (audit and exclusion).

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] An admin POST returns 201 with a `wwt_` token; later GET bodies and the admin_audit row contain neither the token nor its sha256.
- [ ] A viewer POST returns 403; with console.auth=none POST and DELETE return 403 and GET returns 200; the route-coverage test passes with the new routes.
- [ ] DELETE of an id sets revokedAt in the next GET and the token's next /policy request returns 401.
- [ ] One admin audit row is written per create and per revoke, and a heartbeat or ingest POST writes no audit row.
- [ ] `go test -race ./internal/dashboard -run TestWorkerTokensAPI` and `go test -race ./internal/controlplane -run 'TestWorkerTokensAudit|TestAuditSkipsWorkerRoutes'` pass.

### 4/6 · W-P1-WTOK-04

**Add strict worker auth mode and the WARDEN_CP_TOKEN migration guide**

Type **feature** · Size **S** · Issue [#54](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/54)

Add the flags that move a CP from the shared token to per-worker tokens: `--legacy-token-env`, the deprecated `--token-env` alias, `--require-worker-tokens` and `--allow-insecure-worker-auth`. Strict mode rejects the shared token and needs --state-dir and TLS. Legacy use is shown per worker in the fleet view and in a rate-limited warning, since the CP has no metrics endpoint in P1. The migration runbook goes into docs/control-plane.md; recipe changes are W-P1-WTOK-06.

**Requirements**

- `--legacy-token-env` added; `--token-env` kept as an alias marked deprecated with `cmd.Flags().MarkDeprecated`. Setting both to different values is a startup error. Default unset, so behaviour is unchanged.
- `--require-worker-tokens` (default false) needs --state-dir and must not be combined with a legacy token; it needs TLS (--ca-cert/--ca-key) unless `--allow-insecure-worker-auth` is set. Each violation exits non-zero before listening with an error naming the flag.
- Startup logs one line with `auth_mode=open|mixed|strict`, whether a legacy token is configured (never its value), TLS on/off and the active worker token count. Token auth without TLS logs a warning.
- In strict mode with console.auth=none and no legacy token, /central/secrets is not mounted (404) and an error-level line is logged, so the secret-write API never falls back to open.
- Legacy-authenticated requests log `legacy worker token in use` once per proxy id per hour, tracked in a bounded set of 10,000 ids, and increment WorkerView legacyRequests.
- docs/control-plane.md: migration steps (upgrade with --legacy-token-env; create one token per worker; point both controlPlane.tokenEnv and central.tokenEnv at it and set a stable central.proxyID; confirm no legacy badge; restart with --require-worker-tokens; unset the shared env), the rotation flow, prefix binding for replica pools, and revoked-worker behaviour.

**Implementation plan**

1. cmd/proxy/controlplane.go: add the flags and cpOptions fields, the deprecation alias, and the startup validation in runControlPlane.
2. internal/controlplane/controlplane.go: add `Config.RequireWorkerTokens` and `Config.TLS` inputs to the mode resolver; skip mounting /central/secrets in the strict and console.auth=none case.
3. internal/controlplane/workerauth.go: strict mode rejects non-`wwt_` bearers with 401; add the hourly legacy warning with a bounded map and an injectable clock.
4. docs/control-plane.md: add the runbook, rotation and revocation sections.
5. Tests in cmd/proxy/controlplane_test.go (TestControlPlaneAuthFlags) and internal/controlplane/workerauth_test.go.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] With --require-worker-tokens and --state-dir, the shared token gets 401 on /policy, /control/heartbeat and /central/ingest, and the startup log contains `auth_mode=strict`.
- [ ] --require-worker-tokens without --state-dir, with --legacy-token-env, or without TLS and without --allow-insecure-worker-auth exits non-zero before listening, naming the flag.

### 5/6 · W-P1-WTOK-05

**Add offline worker token bootstrap CLI**

Type **feature** · Size **S** · Issue [#235](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/235)

Add `warden control-plane token create|list|revoke` that opens cpstate in --state-dir directly, so the first worker tokens can be created before any admin can log in and while a CP is running. `create --from-env` and `--from-file` register an operator-generated value, which lets compose and Kubernetes Secrets supply tokens without a worker code change. Create and revoke are written to the admin audit log with actor `cli`.

**Requirements**

- `token create --name N (--proxy-id P | --proxy-id-prefix X) [--expires-in D] [--from-env VAR | --from-file F] [--out F]`, `token list [--json]`, `token revoke --id ID`; each takes a required --state-dir and works with or without a running CP.
- Without --from-env/--from-file, create prints the plaintext once to stdout, or writes it to --out with mode 0600 and prints only the id. With an imported value, the plaintext is never printed.
- Imported values must pass the `wwt_` format check. Re-running create with the same name and value is a no-op that exits 0; the same name with a different value exits non-zero.
- Create and revoke append an admin audit row with auth_method `cli` and the OS user when available, holding id, name and binding only.
- Audit appends stay linear when the CP and the CLI write at the same time: the append runs inside a SQLite `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` transaction that reads prev_hash inside it.
- No log line or error contains the plaintext or hash.

**Implementation plan**

1. cmd/proxy/controlplane_token.go (new): newControlPlaneTokenCmd() with create, list and revoke subcommands, added under newControlPlaneCmd() in cmd/proxy/controlplane.go.
2. Each subcommand opens `<state-dir>/warden-cp.db` with cpstate.Open and calls WorkerTokenStore (W-P1-WTOK-01), then closes it.
3. Load the audit key from `--admin-audit-key-file` (default `<state-dir>/cp-audit.key`, never minting a new key when rows exist) and append through adminaudit.Store.Append (W-P1-AAUD-01), which already reads the head and inserts inside one `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` transaction. When the admin_audit table does not exist (admin audit disabled), skip the append and print a one-line notice.
4. Tests in cmd/proxy/controlplane_token_test.go: CLI create against a state dir shared with an httptest CP, import idempotency, --out file mode, and interleaved CLI and in-process audit appends followed by Verify.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] With a CP running on --state-dir D, `warden control-plane token create --name w2 --proxy-id worker-2 --state-dir D --out f` creates f with mode 0600, and a /policy request with its contents gets 200 within 2s and no restart.
- [ ] `WARDEN_WORKER_1_TOKEN=wwt_... warden control-plane token create --name w1 --proxy-id worker-1 --from-env WARDEN_WORKER_1_TOKEN --state-dir D` run twice creates one row; a malformed value exits non-zero.
- [ ] `token revoke --id` on a running CP makes that token's next request return 401 within 2s.
- [ ] After interleaved CLI and API creates and revokes, adminaudit.Verify returns ok and each action appears once with the right actor.
- [ ] `go test -race ./cmd/proxy -run TestControlPlaneTokenCmd` passes.

**Depends on:** [`W-P1-WTOK-01`](worker-credentials.md#16--w-p1-wtok-01) Add worker token store with hashed storage, revocation and in-memory index; [`W-P1-AAUD-01`](admin-audit-log.md#14--w-p1-aaud-01) Add signed, hash-chained admin audit store on cpstate

### 6/6 · W-P1-WTOK-06

**Move compose recipes and worker configs to per-worker tokens**

Type **chore** · Size **S** · Issue [#236](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/236)

Switch the compose recipes and sample worker configs from the shared WARDEN_CP_TOKEN to per-worker tokens. A one-shot bootstrap service registers each worker's token with `token create --from-env` against the shared state volume before workers start, and the CP runs in strict mode. Workers keep reading the token from env, so no worker code changes.

**Requirements**

- deploy/compose/docker-compose.control-plane.yml first, then docker-compose.yml, docker-compose.hermes.yml, docker-compose.openclaw.yml, docker-compose.zeroclaw.yml and docker-compose.ethos.yml (the recipes that pass --token-env), plus the docker-compose.openrouter.yml header comment.
- A one-shot `cp-bootstrap` service runs `control-plane token create --from-env` for each worker against the CP state volume; the CP and workers use `depends_on: condition: service_completed_successfully`.
- Each worker gets its own `WARDEN_WORKER_N_TOKEN`, used by both controlPlane.tokenEnv and central.tokenEnv, and a stable central.proxyID.
- The CP runs with --require-worker-tokens and no WARDEN_CP_TOKEN; recipes keep TLS on.
- configs/config.worker.yaml, config.example-worker.yaml, config.recipe-worker.yaml and config.openrouter-worker.yaml point both tokenEnv keys at the per-worker variable.
- Dev token values come from a documented .env example and are never committed as real secrets.

**Implementation plan**

1. deploy/compose/docker-compose.control-plane.yml: add the cp-bootstrap service on the cp-data volume, switch the CP command to --require-worker-tokens, give worker-1 and worker-2 their own token variables.
2. Apply the same pattern to the other recipes listed above.
3. Update the four configs/config*-worker.yaml files.
4. Update the recipe header comments and docs/control-plane.md quickstart.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] `docker compose -f deploy/compose/docker-compose.control-plane.yml config | grep -c WARDEN_CP_TOKEN` prints 0.
- [ ] After `docker compose -f deploy/compose/docker-compose.control-plane.yml up -d`, GET /dashboard/api/workers lists worker-1 and worker-2 with authKind=token within 30s.
- [ ] Running `docker compose ... up -d` a second time succeeds and does not create new worker_tokens rows.
- [ ] `scripts/check.sh` passes, including `go run docs/roadmap/gen.go check`.
